candidates.name: Hyperparathyroidism-Jaw Tumor Syndrome
support_spans: primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
candidates.why: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, severe hypercalcemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels, combined with the presence of a large tumor on the finger, are consistent with Hyperparathyroidism-Jaw Tumor Syndrome.

candidates.name: Brown Tumor
support_spans: a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
Histopathology of finger tumor
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei and giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers associated with small vessels
candidates.why: The histopathological description of the finger tumor is consistent with a brown tumor, which is a known complication of hyperparathyroidism.

candidates.name: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
support_spans: complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption in the phalangeal tuft band
multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance
candidates.why: The radiographic findings of bone resorption, lytic lesions, and trabecular resorption are consistent with Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica, a condition often associated with hyperparathyroidism.
